bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-01.prompt: How many multiples of $20$ are also divisors of $17!$?

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-02.prompt: Suppose for some positive integers $p,q$ that $\dfrac{p+\frac1q}{q+\frac1p}=17$. What is the greatest integer $n$ such that $\dfrac{p+q}{n}$ is always an integer?

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-03.prompt: Find the minimal $N$ such that any $N$-element subset of $\{1,2,3,4,\dots,7\}$ has a subset $S$ such that the sum of elements of $S$ is divisible by $7$.

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-04.prompt: What is the remainder when $201820182018\ldots$ [$2018$ times] is divided by $15$?

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-05.prompt:
If $r_i$ are integers such that $0\le r_i<31$ and $r_i$ satisfies the polynomial $x^4+x^3+x^2+x\equiv30\pmod{31}$, find
$$\sum_{i=1}^{4}(r_i^2+1)^{-1}\pmod{31}$$
where $x^{-1}$ is the modulo inverse of $x$, that is, it is the unique integer $y$ such that $0<y<31$ and $xy-1$ is divisible by $31$.

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-06.prompt:
Ankit wants to create a pseudo-random number generator using modular arithmetic. To do so he starts with a seed $x_0$ and a function $f(x)=2x+25\pmod{31}$. To compute the $k$th pseudo random number, he calls $g(k)$ defined as follows:
$$g(k)=\begin{cases}x_0&\text{if }k=0\\ f(g(k-1))&\text{if }k>0\end{cases}$$
If $x_0$ is $2017$, compute $\displaystyle\sum_{j=0}^{2017}g(j)\pmod{31}$.

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-07.prompt: Determine the number of ordered triples $(a,b,c)$, with $0\le a,b,c\le10$ for which there exists $(x,y)$ such that $ax^2+by^2\equiv c\pmod{11}$.

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-08.prompt: How many $1<n\le2018$ such that the set $\{0,1,1+2,\dots,1+2+3+\cdots+i,\dots,1+2+\cdots+n-1\}$ is a permutation of $\{0,1,2,3,4,\cdots,n-1\}$ when reduced modulo $n$?

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-09.prompt:
Compute the following:
$$\sum_{x=0}^{99}(x^2+1)^{-1}\pmod{199}$$
where $x^{-1}$ is the value $0\le y\le199$ such that $xy-1$ is divisible by $199$.
